As fall arrives in Maine, respiratory viruses such as influenza (flu), COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), also return and begin to spread more widely as people spend more time together, indoors. The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) reminds Maine people and visitors to take steps to keep themselves, their loved ones, and neighbors healthy this respiratory virus season.
Respiratory viruses can cause fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle aches, and fatigue. Some people are more likely to get very sick and need medical attention. These viruses can spread when an infected person coughs or sneezes. They can also spread from touching the surface with the virus on it and then touching your nose or mouth before washing your hands.

recommends

Wash your hands frequently with soap and water.
Clean and disinfect surfaces and objects that people touch often.
If you are sick, consider wearing a mask around others.
Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or your elbow.
Avoid close contact with people who are sick.
Get vaccinated, as appropriate for flu, COVID-19, and RSV.
Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent respiratory viruses. Vaccines can also help make illness less severe and help prevent missed work or school. Sep 25, 2026

As fall arrives in Maine, respiratory viruses such as influenza (flu), COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), also return and begin to spread more widely as people spend more time together, indoors. The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) reminds Maine people and visitors to take steps to keep themselves, their loved ones, and neighbors healthy this respiratory virus season.

Respiratory viruses can cause fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle aches, and fatigue. Some people are more likely to get very sick and need medical attention. These viruses can spread when an infected person coughs or sneezes. They can also spread from touching the surface with the virus on it and then touching your nose or mouth before washing your hands.

The Maine CDC recommends the following measures to protect yourself and others:

  • Stay home when you are sick.
  • Wash your hands frequently with soap and water.
  • Clean and disinfect surfaces and objects that people touch often.
  • If you are sick, consider wearing a mask around others.
  • Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or your elbow.
  • Avoid close contact with people who are sick.
  • Get vaccinated, as appropriate for flu, COVID-19, and RSV.

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent respiratory viruses. Vaccines can also help make illness less severe and help prevent missed work or school. Getting a flu vaccine every year and staying up to date with COVID-19 and RSV vaccinations, if eligible, can help lower the risk of getting sick.

Consistent with the recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, the Maine CDC recommends the following respiratory virus immunization for the 2026-2027 season:

  • Flu: Everyone 6 months and older should receive an annual flu vaccine.
  • COVID-19: Vaccination is recommended for
    • all children ages 6 through 23 months;
    • children and adolescents ages 2 through 18 years who are at increased risk for severe COVID-19 or who want to be vaccinated;
    • adults age 19 and older;
    • pregnant individuals.
  • RSV: Immunization is recommended for certain infants, pregnant people, and older adults.
    • Infants: RSV immunization is recommended for those younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, if they are not protected by maternal RSV vaccination.
      • Certain children ages 8-19 months who are at increased risk for severe RSV may also be recommended to receive RSV immunization during their second season.
    • Pregnant people: RSV vaccination is recommended during weeks 32 through 36 of pregnancy.
    • Older adults: All adults age 75 and older and adults 50-74 at increased risk for severe RSV illness.

To find the nearest location to get a vaccine, contact your local pharmacy or health care provider.

items.title: US Department of Labor releases new workplace guidance to prepare employers, workers for opioid emergencies

The fact sheet provides practical information that focuses on empowering workplaces to recognize the signs of an overdose and act immediately.“President Trump has charged the Department of Labor with making recovery part of our workforce strategy, helping more individuals return to work and ensuring our businesses have the workers they need,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Today’s guidance, released as part of President Trump’s Great American Recovery Initiative, is exactly the kind of action we were tasked with delivering on for the American people.”“President Trump has been fighting back against the deadly synthetic opioids infecting the entire illicit drug supply, from known illicit drugs to counterfeit tablets sold on the street or through fake online pharmacies,” said White House Drug Czar Sara Carter. “Because fentanyl has infiltrated the illicit drug landscape and acts as a chemical weapon against our people, it is critically important that the American workforce is familiar with drug overdose recognition and reversal. I am grateful to the Department of Labor for informing employers and workers about life-saving overdose reversal treatments like naloxone.”OSHA’s fact sheet highlights key opioid overdose preparedness strategies, including:Keep lifesaving FDA-approved reversal medications – such as naloxone or nalmefene – on hand. These safe, life-saving medications quickly restore normal breathing and generally have no effect if opioids are not present.Treat overdose kits like first aid by storing them in highly visible, easily accessible locations, just like automated external defibrillators or standard first-aid kits.Educate workers on how to identify critical symptoms of an overdose, such as slow or stopped breathing, blue lips or skin, pinpoint pupils, or unresponsiveness.Prepare for rapid action in an emergency by training workers to administer the medication, safely position the individual, and provide supportive care while waiting for first responders.OSHA’s guidance emphasizes that while these medications are critical, they do not replace emergency services. Workplace responders should always call 911 immediately because the medication’s effects are temporary and professional medical care is still required.The Department of Labor is committed to supporting workers’ safety and health on the job, along with partners at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and other agencies.Read the Opioid Overdose Rescue with Reversal Medications fact sheet.Learn more about OSHA.

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor offers free workplace safety and labor law training to help employers, managers, supervisors, human resources professionals and others understand workplace safety requirements and Maine labor laws. The Department has announced its schedule of October classes, with trainings offered through SafetyWorks! and the Bureau of Labor Standards.

Registration is required, and space may be limited. View the October schedule and register for a class.

Unless otherwise noted, classes are held at the SafetyWorks! Training Institute at the Maine Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive in Augusta.

October Class Schedule

Fire Extinguisher/Emergency Action Plans/Workplace Violence Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Workplace emergencies include fire, medical, and workplace violence. This course covers the requirements of an emergency action plan, fire extinguisher use, and considering the potential for workplace violence. The SWTI Lab includes a fire extinguisher discharge activity to assist participants in learning how to use a fire extinguisher.

Bloodborne Pathogens Train-the-Trainer Friday, Oct. 2, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

This half-day class provides guidance on what is needed to be compliant with the bloodborne pathogen standard. This course will review written program requirements, training, documentation, Hepatitis B, and sharp logs.

Successful safety and health programs are more than just compliance with the OSHA standards. Injuries and illnesses are reduced when employers possess common elements to identify and address safety and health hazards. This course outlines roles and responsibilities, common principles, required functions and programs of a successful safety and health management system. This course prepares organizations who would like to pursue SHARP/ SHAPE.

Cold & Heat Illness Prevention Friday, Oct. 9, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Whether your employees work outside or inside, cold and hot temperatures can be hazardous to their health. This class covers cold and heat temperature illnesses, signs and symptoms, and control measures to prevent and treat temperature related injuries.

items.title: US Department of Labor cites Florida pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards after March fatality
items.content_text: ORLANDO, FL – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an Orlando-based pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing employees to safety hazards after an incident claimed the life of a worker at a New Smyrna Beach worksite in March 2026.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that on March 17, 2026, T & T Pipeline Co. Inc. employees were replacing a drill bit on a horizontal drilling machine when the pipe stem began to rotate and fatally struck the employee.OSHA cited the employer with a willful violation for exposing employees to struck-by hazards when working on a horizontal directional drilling machine and proposed $165,514 in penalties. The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

items.title: US Department of Labor cites New Jersey car wash for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards, proposes more than $446K in fines
items.content_text: SICKLERVILLE, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a New Jersey car wash service for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards related to hazardous energy and excessive noise levels, proposing $446,864 in penalties.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that ModWash LLC, an express car wash service operating multiple locations throughout the country, including five in Sicklerville, willfully exposed workers to hazardous energy by failing to lock out equipment prior to conducting maintenance activities and not using energy control procedures. The agency also cited ModWash for two repeat violations for failing to have clear lockout procedures and specific instructions for controlling all energy sources and not training employees on equipment lockout/tagout processes. In addition, the employer was cited for five serious violations for failing to develop and implement a noise monitoring program, establish a baseline audiogram for employees within six months of exposure, train employees exposed to noise above 85 decibels, provide lockout/tagout devices, and attach such devices to machines prior to servicing them.The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Sep 21, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 21, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles:   

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

  *As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines. 

Other system access limitations: 

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 21, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.  

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 21, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

Maine's Minimum Wage to Increase to $15.70 Per Hour in 2027

September 18, 2026

For Immediate Release: September 18, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor announced today that, effective January 1, 2027, the state minimum wage will increase from $15.10 to $15.70 per hour, based on data recently made available by the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics. MDOL is required under Maine law (Maine statute Title 26, chapter 7, section 664) to make annual adjustments to the minimum wage based on the cost-of-living index (CPI-W) for the Northeast Region, after Maine voters amended the law by referendum in 2016. Between August 2025 and August 2026, there was a 4.1 percent increase in the CPI-W.

According to the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Population Survey for 2025, there were 28,000 hourly workers who were paid less than $15.00 per hour. These workers represent about four percent of all wage and salary workers (both paid at hourly rates and not paid at hourly rates) and about eight percent of wage and salary workers who are paid at hourly rates.

Agricultural workers in Maine are also entitled to the state minimum wage, after the Legislature enacted and Governor Mills signed "An Act to Establish a State Minimum Hourly Wage for Agricultural Workers" in 2025.

The "tip wage," or service employee minimum wage, will increase from $7.55 to $7.85 per hour. This means that service employees must receive a direct cash wage of at least $7.85 per hour from the employer. The employer must be able to show that the employee receives at least the minimum wage of $15.70 per hour when the direct wage and tips are combined at the end of the week. The amount of tips necessary to qualify as a service employee will increase from $191 to $199 per month.

The minimum salary threshold for exempting a worker from overtime pay must exceed 3,000 times the State's minimum wage or the annualized rate established by the U.S. Department of Labor, whichever is higher. Starting January 1, 2027, the new minimum salary threshold for salaried workers exempt from overtime will be $905.79 per week, or $47,101.08 per year. This is only one of the factors used in determining whether a worker is exempt from overtime pay under federal or state law. An individual can earn more than the minimum salary threshold and still be eligible for overtime. The duties of each worker must be considered as part of this analysis.

Employers can download the required minimum wage poster at no cost on the Department's website.

The minimum wage and overtime law can be found here.

Measles is a highly contagious viral disease. If one person has measles, 90% of the people close to that person who are not immune will become infected. Symptoms of measles include:

  • Fever

Individuals who develop symptoms should contact their health care provider for instructions before going to the provider’s office or hospital. This will help prevent the spread of further infection. If symptoms are consistent with measles, a health care professional may test to determine a measles infection.

Measles can cause severe sickness including pneumonia, encephalitis (brain swelling), and death. An infected person spreads measles through coughs or sneezes. Once infected, a person is contagious from four days before their rash starts through four days afterwards. The virus remains alive for up to two hours on surfaces and in the air. The period from exposure to onset of symptoms is typically 10 to 14 days, but can be longer.

The measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine is the best prevention for measles. Individuals who:   

  • have been potentially exposed should review their vaccine history and watch for symptoms.
  • are not immunized or do not know their measles immunization status should get vaccinated.
  • develop symptoms should contact their health provider for instructions before going to the provider’s office or hospital. This will help prevent the spread of further infection.

  • Children – Identify and vaccinate children who are not up to date with their MMR vaccines. All children should receive two doses of MMR vaccine. A health care professional should administer the first dose to children at 12 to 15 months old and the second at 4 to 6 years old.
    • Children 6 to 11 months old who will be traveling internationally or domestically to a region with a known active measles outbreak should receive one dose of MMR vaccine, per the Maine CDC’s expanded recommendations for those traveling to a destination with a known outbreak. This dose is not considered part of the routine two-dose series starting at age 12 months.  
  • Adults – All adults should have proof of immunity to measles. Acceptable proof includes one of the following:
    • written documentation of vaccination
    • laboratory evidence of immunity
    • birth before 1957
    • or laboratory confirmation of disease
    • individuals who received a measles vaccine between 1963 to 1967 are encouraged to speak with their doctor to determine if additional vaccination is needed. Those known to have received an inactivated dose measles vaccine should receive a single dose of MMR. Five percent of people who received measles vaccine between 1963 and 1967 received an inactivated vaccine.

For adults with no evidence of immunity to measles, the U.S. CDC recommends one dose of MMR vaccine as soon as possible. Adults who are traveling domestically or internationally to a region known to have an active measles outbreak should receive two doses of the vaccine. Pregnant women should not receive any live virus vaccine during pregnancy, including MMR.

Vaccination Information:

  • Two doses of MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles; one dose is about 93% effective.
  • The U.S. CDC considers people who received two doses of MMR vaccine as a child protected for life. 
  • Some people exposed to the virus may still get measles even if they got the MMR vaccine. In this case, they are more likely to have a milder illness and are also less likely to spread the disease to other people.

For More Information:

  • The Maine CDC’s measles webpage: http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/measles
  • The U.S. CDC’s measles webpage: http://www.cdc.gov/measles/index.html
  • The Maine Immunization Program webpage: https://www.maine.gov/dhhs/mecdc/infectious-disease/immunization/

items.title: US Department of Labor investigation finds Chicago construction employer exposed workers to continued safety hazards, proposes $265K in penalties
items.content_text: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Calumet City-based residential construction and carpentry employer after two separate investigations into its continued failure to provide fall protection for workers. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration investigated two worksites operated by Martin Araujo – doing business as Araujo Construction Corp. – and found that carpenters and general construction laborers were installing roof rafters and roof sheeting without fall protection, exposing them to falls of up to 25 feet. OSHA cited Araujo Construction with two willful violations for not providing fall protection, while working from heights during residential construction at the two worksites. OSHA also cited the employer with nine repeat safety violations for failing to provide head and eye protection, lacking handrails on stairways, and failing to make sure ladders extended three feet above access areas. Additionally, OSHA issued a serious violation to Araujo Construction for not having safe access to a platform, and an other-than-serious violation for lacking training certifications. OSHA proposed $265,868 in combined penalties.Martin Araujo has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.  Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, employers are responsible for providing safe and healthful workplaces for their employees. OSHA’s role is to ensure these conditions for America’s working men and women by setting and enforcing standards, and providing training, education and assistance. See OSHA’s website for more information.

WHEREAS
, food is one of Maine’s most valuable resources and is essential for the health and nutrition of all our 1.4 million residents; and
WHEREAS
, nearly 40 percent of food produced in Maine is never eaten – over 361,000 tons annually – primarily ending up in landfills where it produces dangerous methane gas which is 28 times more potent than carbon dioxide and a major contributor to climate change; and
WHEREAS
, Maine people can save money by preventing wasted food, with the average Maine family spending nearly $3,000 annually on food that is thrown away; and
WHEREAS
, over 80 percent of consumers misunderstand food date labels causing large amounts of perfectly good food to be thrown away in homes, businesses, and even food pantries; and
WHEREAS
, Maine communities can substantially reduce their waste disposal costs by preventing wasted food since food is the single largest municipal solid waste component; and
WHEREAS
, Maine K-12 schools have a special role in educating our next generation to reduce, recover, and recycle the estimated 7 million pounds of school food wasted annually; and
WHEREAS
, we can help our farmers, strengthen our local food systems, and conserve our natural resources – water, air, energy, and land – by valuing Maine food and composting food scraps instead of wasting it as trash;

Maine Wasted Food Prevention Week
and I encourage all Maine people to become aware of the wasted food in our homes, schools and all around us, and to commit to stop throwing food away.

By strengthening pre-apprenticeship programs and giving employers the guidance and tools necessary to funnel younger workers into registered apprenticeship programs, the Trump Administration is ensuring the American workforce gains and maintains the skills necessary to build the modern and future economy. ETA also issued Circular 2026-04, informing employers that sponsor registered apprentices how to obtain money made available through the new Workforce Pell Grant, created by the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. By following this guidance and partnering with eligible educational institutions, employers using registered apprentices can access program flexibilities that allow businesses to grow and apprentices to build a high-paying career in their communities.ETA published Unemployment Insurance Program Letter 14-26, furthering President Trump’s directive to fight fraud by setting expectations for state workforce agencies to develop and implement plans to combat fraud in their state-level unemployment insurance systems and clarifying when states must adopt corrective action plans for failure to protect against the misuse of American’s tax dollars.  Bureau of International Labor Affairs:ILAB released videos highlighting the American stories that put our workers front and center. Each story makes it clear President Trump’s work is increasing U.S. job and wage growth, enforcing fair labor standards, and backing American workers and businesses with the tools they need to compete and win.Mine Safety and Health Administration:Aiming to achieve greater consistency of outcomes, MSHA recently centralized its negotiators into the Conference Litigation and Investigative Resources group. This new structure will streamline conferences, reduce litigation costs, and enhance agency credibility before judges, operators, and miners. This will help support the Trump administration’s reinvigoration of the American coal industry.MSHA recently launched a new, comprehensive “professionalism” training course for inspectors, as well as managers and administrative staff in the field who also interact with the public. To kick off the week, the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened will hold its 35th Annual Tea in Celebration of Deaf Culture Week on Sept. 17, from 2 to 4 p.m. at the Hall of Flags in the State House in Augusta. The event is open to the public.

Clayton Marr III will give the keynote address. Marr grew up in Westbrook and currently lives in Knoxville, Tenn. where he is the student activity coordinator for the Tennessee Schools for the Deaf. He works with Deaf students to support their academic success, personal growth, and independence.

"Maine's Deaf community has enriched our state for generations through its language, culture, traditions and contributions. I've proudly declared September 20-26 as Deaf Culture Week in celebration of that heritage and the Deaf and hard-of-hearing Mainers who make our state a better place," said Governor Mills.

"The Maine Department of Labor is proud to support the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened and this 35th annual celebration of Deaf culture. I encourage Maine employers to harness the many skills and experiences of people with disabilities. MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Sep 08, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 08, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that begins September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink. 

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access
